examples.english: I want to erase these hateful memories.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{忌々|いまいま}しそう⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{舌打|したう}ち→舌打ち：14982_shitauchi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: He clicked his tongue in irritation.

notes:
{忌々|いまいま}しい is an i-adjective expressing strong irritation or vexation.

ETYMOLOGY:
- From {忌|い}む (to avoid, detest) - something so unpleasant one wants to avoid it

INTENSITY:
- Stronger than うっとうしい (annoying) or ⟦{面倒|めんどう}→面倒：03809_mendou⟧ (troublesome)
- Expresses genuine anger or hatred, not just mild annoyance
- Often used when something repeatedly frustrates you

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {忌々|いまいま}しそう⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧ (with an irritated look)
- {忌々|いまいま}しい⟦{記憶|きおく}→記憶：00234_kioku⟧/⟦{思|おも}い{出|で}→思い出：00331_omoide⟧ (hateful memories)
- {忌々|いまいま}しい⟦{限|かぎ}り→限り：00133_kagiri⟧ (extremely annoying)

USAGE:
- Describing people, situations, or things that cause persistent frustration
- Often used in internal monologue or when venting
- Can describe memories or past events that still irritate

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{腹立|はらだ}たしい→腹立たしい：21455_haradatashii⟧: Irritating (makes you angry)
- うっとうしい: Annoying (bothersome)
- {忌々|いまいま}しい: Hateful, infuriating (stronger, with resentment)

REGISTER: Neutral to informal. Expresses strong emotion.
